solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Marvellous surroundings for quiet meal

indicators.note: the first word's letters wrap around the next piece, as surroundings enclose something

parts.note: marvellous means super
P (piano) is the musical abbreviation for quiet

explanation.surface: Someone praises a lovely setting for a peaceful dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: An evening repast, especially a light late one, is called this.

clue.text: Takes Mickey — to prison?

definitions.meaning: taking the mickey is mocking or parodying someone
being sent up is slang for being jailed

explanation.surface: Someone mocks a man called Mickey and then jails him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes the mickey' is British slang for mocking.
explanation.definitionFit: To parody someone, and also slang for committing a person to jail.

clue.text: Wonders when phone exchange changed name

indicators.note: exchange and changed both say the letters are swapped around into a new order

explanation.surface: A telephone exchange was renamed, to everyone's amazement.
explanation.definitionFit: Marvels or remarkable occurrences, the plural of a striking event.

clue.text: Excuse may mean the taxman may ignore some charge

definitions.meaning: to excuse someone is to free them from a duty

definitions.text: the taxman may ignore some charge
definitions.meaning: a charge free from tax is one the revenue does not levy

explanation.surface: A justification might mean the tax office overlooks a fee.
explanation.definitionFit: To free from an obligation, and also not liable to a levy.

clue.text: Sweetheart joins sergeant in dance

parts.note: an old flame is a sweetheart
a sergeant is an NCO, a non-commissioned officer

explanation.surface: A lover partners an army sergeant on the dance floor.
explanation.definitionFit: A passionate Spanish gypsy dance, a named example of dancing.

clue.text: Part of fingerprint found — the game's up!

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: pool is a cue game

explanation.surface: A detective finds a print and announces the game is up.
explanation.definitionFit: A whorl-like ridge pattern is one of the basic print types.

clue.text: Dissipated female locked up

parts.note: a miss is a young woman
pent means confined or shut up

explanation.surface: A dissolute woman is imprisoned.
explanation.definitionFit: Wasted or squandered, as a dissolute youth is frittered away.

clue.text: Mr Runyan has to be put up, being domestically unstable

indicators.note: in a down clue put up means the name is written upwards, reversed

parts.note: Damon Runyon was the American writer of Guys and Dolls stories

explanation.surface: A writer needs lodging, being without a settled home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' looks like giving lodging; it turns the first name around.
explanation.definitionFit: A wanderer with no fixed home lives without a settled dwelling.

clue.text: Exercise supervision in place of a bishop

definitions.meaning: read as over plus see, being in authority over a bishop's diocese

explanation.surface: Someone takes charge while standing in for a bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: A see is a bishop's diocese; to be over a see is to be in charge of it.
explanation.definitionFit: To supervise or watch over work is to manage it.

clue.text: Relatives might make a scene about one

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the next piece, as about means around
the letters of scene might be made into something else, so they are rearranged

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Family members could cause a fuss in public over someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might make' turns SCENE into NECES, and 'about' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Daughters of one's siblings are family members, hence kin.

clue.text: Study battle — when it's clear of course

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn
the Somme was a First World War battle

explanation.surface: A student reads up on a battle, wondering when matters will become clear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of course' means a course of a meal: the answer is a clear soup.
explanation.definitionFit: A clarified meat soup served as one course of a meal.

clue.text: Well-known Russian cocktail

definitions.meaning: Vyacheslav ... was a Soviet foreign minister
a petrol bomb is named a cocktail after him

explanation.surface: A famous Russian mixed drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A Soviet statesman, whose name was given to an improvised petrol bomb.

clue.text: Small creature aggressively reared

parts.note: an arachnid raises its stinging tail over its back in threat, so it is a little animal that rears up aggressively

explanation.surface: A tiny animal was brought up to be fierce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reared' looks like upbringing but means raised up, as this creature lifts its tail to strike.
explanation.definitionFit: This stinging arachnid is a small animal famous for its raised tail.

clue.text: They may turn up trumps sometimes

definitions.text: They may turn up trumps sometimes

parts.words: They may turn up trumps sometimes
parts.note: garden tools turn up soil, and a card suit is sometimes the trump suit

explanation.surface: Some things prove unexpectedly helpful now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn up trumps' is the idiom for doing well unexpectedly; here digging tools turn up earth and a card suit can be trumps.
explanation.definitionFit: Both digging tools and a suit of playing cards, which can be named trumps.

clue.text: A lover — married, unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests the letters of married have gone wrong and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A suitor turns out to have a wife already, alas.
explanation.definitionFit: A fan or suitor who loves someone.

clue.text: An ode for author getting married

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe was an American author

explanation.surface: A writer composes verse on the occasion of a wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: An ode is a kind of lyric verse composition.

clue.text: One may put one's foot in it — how does one wriggle out?

definitions.text: One may put one's foot in it

indicators.note: the words how does one wriggle into a new order, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Someone who has made a tactless remark asks how to escape the consequences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put one's foot in it' means blunder, but here literally a foot goes inside the item.
explanation.definitionFit: A clog or sabot is footwear one literally places one's foot inside.

clue.text: We are all involved in mortal competition

parts.note: mortal means human
a race is a competition

explanation.surface: Everyone takes part in a deadly contest.
explanation.definitionFit: Humankind is the group to which every person belongs.

clue.text: The provision of a home for a small charge

definitions.text: The provision of a home for a small charge

parts.words: The provision of a home for a small charge
parts.note: a small charge is a child in one's care, and giving it a home is taking it in as one's own

explanation.surface: Lodging is offered for a modest fee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small charge' looks like a low price; it is a child in someone's care.
explanation.definitionFit: Legally taking a child into one's family as one's own.

clue.text: Being upright has prospect of success

definitions.meaning: standing on one's feet, with the clue reading the phrase as a stance taken for victory
to be in line to gain or come out ahead

explanation.surface: Standing firm gives one a chance of victory.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue leans on two senses of stand: being on one's feet, and being placed to gain.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in line to gain something is an idiom for likely victory.

clue.text: Grows vegetables — from Brussels?

definitions.meaning: to sprout is to begin to grow

explanation.surface: Someone grows vegetables from Belgium.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoots up, and small green cabbage-like vegetables named after Brussels.

clue.text: Ancient Mariner's story brought back by Arab prince

indicators.note: brought back means the word is read from the end towards the start

parts.note: Coleridge's poem is The Rime of the Ancient Mariner

explanation.surface: An Arab ruler returns the tale of a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: A title for a Muslim ruler or commander, especially in Arab lands.

clue.text: Book is in stock

definitions.meaning: to book is to engage in advance
a stock is a supply held back for later

explanation.surface: A book is held in a shop's stock.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrange in advance, and also a supply kept back.

clue.text: Yet such talkers may not be on the level

definitions.text: Yet such talkers may not be on the level

parts.words: Yet such talkers may not be on the level
parts.note: glib persuasive speakers are not honest, though the word for them also means flat and level

explanation.surface: Persuasive speakers may not be honest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the level' means honest; the paradox is that the adjective for glib talkers also means flat.
explanation.definitionFit: Glib and suave, as a slick talker is, though it also means flat.

clue.text: Make another impression in the pool?

definitions.text: Make another impression in the pool?

parts.words: Make another impression in the pool?
parts.note: a typist in an office typing pool keys the text again, making a second impression on paper

explanation.surface: Someone wants to leave a second mark at the swimming baths.
explanation.walkthrough: The pool is an office typing pool, not a swimming pool.
explanation.definitionFit: To key text in again produces a fresh printed impression.

clue.text: A stunning police device

parts.note: an electric stun gun used by police officers, stunning in the literal sense

explanation.surface: Police have an impressive gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stunning' looks like impressive; it is literal, a weapon that stuns.
explanation.definitionFit: An electroshock weapon carried by police to incapacitate suspects.

clue.text: End of semester in America

parts.note: a semester is an academic term
taken as written
US is America

explanation.surface: The close of the academic half-year in an American college.
explanation.definitionFit: A final stop of a railway or bus line, the end of the route.

clue.text: Exploit a twist of fate

indicators.note: a twist of says the letters of fate are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: Taking advantage of an unexpected turn of fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: A notable deed or achievement, an exploit used as a noun.

clue.text: Being married holds us back if incompatible

indicators.note: holds means the first word's letters contain the next piece

parts.note: being married is being united

indicators.note: back means the word us is read backwards

explanation.surface: A marriage keeps two people back if they don't get on.
explanation.definitionFit: Not well matched or not fitted, as two ill-matched people are.

clue.text: Doctor goes to hospital to look for material

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor
an air is a look or appearance

explanation.surface: A physician visits a hospital to find some fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A fabric made from Angora goat hair, so a kind of cloth.

clue.text: Musical composition for an Easter service

indicators.note: service suggests the letters being worked over and put in a new order

explanation.surface: A piece of music written for a church Easter service.
explanation.definitionFit: A light orchestral piece, a type of musical composition akin to a serenade.

clue.text: Scheme to expire

definitions.meaning: to expire is to breathe out, here noisily and with a whistle

explanation.surface: Plotting to die.
explanation.definitionFit: A clever plan, and also to breathe out with a rasping whistle.
